Then we will be able to inform you of our position next week. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have two days until the beginning of next week. As you have said, you spent 15 days to examine the lists. There are documents that you could assess, and you should be able to know which documents will be subject to a debate and which documents could be admitted into evidence. But as you have said, it's necessary to make a distinction between the relevance and the probative value of a document. And sometimes the Trial Chamber has the impression that the parties are confusing these two issues. The fact that a document is admitted into evidence does not mean that this document has been given certain probative weight. A document is assessed on the basis of the quality of its source, the witness, the context, the contents of the document, various testimonies, et cetera, and this is a matter for the Trial Chamber to determine. So I wanted to point this out to you. It would be best for you to think about the matter and on Monday we will take stock of the subject. Mr. Withopf, are there any other comments to be made?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. President and Your Honours. It sounds awful submitting a document of about 300 pages. I think this issue is not that difficult. The Defence in their own submission have identified a number of criteria why they think 650 documents have to be challenged from their point of view. If they apply these criteria to the documents, it could be done in a sort of a tick box. Actually, document number 1, translation issue. Document number 2, ceding authority. And in very brief, in some sort of a bullet-point form, a very brief explanation could be given. I don't think 300 pages are necessary. Secondly, we have during the week after Easter we don't have court sessions, which would allow the Defence to work on this issue. There's a full week in order to cover all these issues. And I still think - and that's at least the conclusion I've drawn from the Defence submission, that they've made up their minds in respect to each and every document - it doesn't appear too complicated to cover this issue within two weeks, one week of the two weeks being no court session. Again, it appears to be highly problematic to revisit the very same issue again and again and again after a decision has been made. We are too far in the course of this trial, and we are actually in -- within two months the Prosecution will finish the presentation of its case to -- not to know how the parties or how the Prosecution is obliged to tender its documents. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, you have the floor for the last time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have serious reservations regarding the statement made by my learned friend from the Prosecution. Who is he to know how much time we need for what we are to do and what we're going to say about our documents and about our decisions? We believe that it is quite unacceptable, Mr. President. The question of documents is a question that we will attach full importance to; however, we need time to evaluate, to assess our position in order to protect the position of the accused, and that is our duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In any event, we have the weekend, which will give you time to think things over and for your positions to mature, bearing in mind that the procedure that applies to the Prosecution, to which the Defence naturally has to react, will in the future also apply to the Prosecution when the Defence produces its documents. So there is an equality of arms in that respect that is fully observed. In the interest of economy, we need to develop a system when documents that are tendered or will be tendered should be done in the most appropriate manner without any useless debate, which takes time away from the testimony. Because that is after all important, because our procedure is based on oral testimony. And we shouldn't allow these debates on documents to detract from the time we devote to those testimonies. Therefore, you will have two days to think things over. We will start the hearing on Monday by addressing this question once again. If there are no other matters, I thank both parties and all those present, and I invite you to come back here on Monday at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of April, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.26 a.m.,
